explanation: One of Jesus' twelve disciples who here tells the Jerusalem church about his experience with Cornelius.
A Roman centurion (officer) from Caesarea who was a God-fearing Gentile and received God's word through Peter's vision.
An revealed sight or dream in which God communicated to both Cornelius, instructing him to send for Peter, and to Peter, breaking down the barrier between Jews and Gentiles.
A person who is not Jewish; in this context, it refers to people outside the Jewish covenant who were now included in God's kingdom through faith in Jesus.
The ritual act with water by which newly converted Gentiles, after receiving the Holy Spirit, publicly affirmed their faith and joined the church.
The community of believing Christians gathered to listen to Peter's account that God's grace had also been given to the Gentiles.
